stage_description: Load task, initialize browser/desktop/container/API environment, restore initial state.
resource_signature: Environment-bound startup cost; often hidden by benchmark papers but important in multi-tenant scheduling.

stage_description: Agent reads user goal, policy, tools, previous state, and forms an initial plan.
resource_signature: LLM prefill/decode dominated; HBM/KV pressure grows with policy/tool/context length.

stage_description: Agent receives webpage, screenshot, desktop state, terminal output, or API/user message.
resource_signature: Observation modality determines resource shift: GUI/web creates screenshot/DOM/network pressure; tool/API creates smaller text observations.

stage_description: Parse DOM/logs/files, OCR or visually ground screenshot, retrieve/search local context.
resource_signature: Mixed accelerator+CPU+memory phase; strongest evidence for non-LLM heterogeneous hardware demand.

stage_description: LLM chooses next tool/API/browser/GUI/terminal action and arguments.
resource_signature: Accelerator-centric but sensitive to context size and number of tools/actions.

stage_description: Execute selected action: click/type/navigate, call API tool, run command, edit file, update DB.
resource_signature: Device demand fans out by flow type: network for API/web, CPU/storage for terminal/code, display stack for GUI.

stage_description: Wait for page load, API response, command/test completion, file generation, or app state update.
resource_signature: Burst phase; good target for resource disaggregation and co-location with LLM-bound tenants.

stage_description: Read errors, retry, backtrack, regenerate arguments, or repair a failed action.
resource_signature: Long-tail resource amplifier; repeated loops convert small task errors into large accelerator/network/CPU waste.

stage_description: Run evaluator, compare final state, save artifacts, emit answer.
resource_signature: Often CPU/storage/container-heavy; essential for measuring real flow completion rather than model-only latency.
